Scout, in motion

Your four renders, cut out of the checkerboard and rigged with CSS motion. Nothing here is a new frame — it's transform-based life: float, breathe, sway, perk, pop, and a cross-fade between poses.

What CSS can and can't do

Can: move, rotate, scale, skew, fade and cross-fade the whole image — enough to make a static render feel alive and responsive to app state.

Can't: move the tail independently, blink, or change expression. Those need either separate layered renders, a frame sequence, or a rigged Rive/Lottie file.

Motion lab

Five primitives, each mapped to an app state. Combine two at most — float plus breathe reads alive; float plus breathe plus sway reads seasick.

Float

The default idle. 9px vertical, 4.4s, shadow scales inversely.

@keyframes float

Breathe

1.4% scale, anchored at the feet. Barely visible, does most of the work.

@keyframes breathe

Sway

±2.3° from the hips. Fakes the weight of the tail without moving it.

@keyframes sway

Perk

Idle, then a startle every few seconds. For expiry warnings.

@keyframes alertPerk

Cross-fade

Pose swap on state change. Waving → holding the acorn.

@keyframes crossfade

In the app

Same layout and palette you signed off on. Scout floats in the empty state, perks in the alert card, and sits still as a cropped headshot in the app bar.

Production notes

Asset issues to fix

  • These weren't transparent. The upload was flat RGB with the checkerboard baked in as pixels — I keyed it out, but re-export as real PNG-32 with alpha and you'll get clean fur edges instead of my approximation.
  • Lighting is inconsistent. The acorn pose is lit from the front, the alert pose from the left. Regenerate with a fixed light direction or they'll read as different animals.
  • Scale drift. Head-to-body ratio differs across the four. Lock a character reference before generating more poses.

If you want real motion

  • Layered renders. Ask for tail, body and head as separate transparent images, then animate each layer. Cheapest path to a moving tail.
  • Rive. Best fit for an app — small files, runtime state machine, hooks into your warranty state. Needs an animator.
  • AI video (Runway, Kling, Pika) can animate a still, but output is video, not transparent, and won't loop cleanly. Wrong tool for UI.
  • Frame sequence. Generate 4–6 poses of the same action and flip through them with steps(). Cheap, but consistency across frames is hard to get from image models.
